Given data: Line voltage ($V_L$) = $400\text{ V}$, Frequency ($f$) = $50\text{ Hz}$, Line current ($I_L$) = $17.32\text{ A}$, Power factor ($\cos\phi$) = $0.8$ (lagging), Connection = Delta.

**(i) Phase current ($I_{ph}$):**
For a delta-connected system:
$$I_L = \sqrt{3} I_{ph}$$
$$I_{ph} = \frac{I_L}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{17.32}{\sqrt{3}} = 10\text{ A}$|

**(ii) Resistance ($R$) and Inductance ($L$) of each coil:**
Phase voltage ($V_{ph}$) = Line voltage ($V_L$) = $400\text{ V}$
Impedance per phase ($Z_{ph}$) = $\frac{V_{ph}}{I_{ph}} = \frac{400}{10} = 40\text{ }\Omega$

Resistance ($R$) = $Z_{ph} \cos\phi = 40 \times 0.8 = 32\text{ }\Omega$

Reactance ($X_L$) = $Z_{ph} \sin\phi = 40 \times \sin(\arccos(0.8)) = 40 \times 0.6 = 24\text{ }\Omega$

Inductance ($L$) = $\frac{X_L}{2 \pi f} = \frac{24}{2 \times \pi \times 50} = 0.0764\text{ H}$ or $76.4\text{ mH}$

**(iii) Power drawn by each coil ($P_{ph}$):**
$$P_{ph} = V_{ph} I_{ph} \cos\phi = 400 \times 10 \times 0.8 = 3200\text{ W} = 3.2\text{ kW}$$
proTip: Remember that in a delta connection, phase voltage equals line voltage, but line current is $\sqrt{3}$ times the phase current.
